paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: real greatness picks up the towel. Jesus knew the Father had delivered all things into His hands, and He knew He had come from God and was returning to God (John 13:3). Then He got down and washed feet. Nobody at that table could say love like that was beneath Him, because He was their Lord and Teacher and He did it anyway (John 13:13-14).

Now here's why it matters to YOU. Peter first said, "Never shall You wash my feet!" and Jesus answered, "Unless I wash you, you have no part with Me" (John 13:8). Friend, we all want to hand Jesus our best and keep the messy parts out of sight, but being served by Him comes first, so you don't earn the towel, you receive it. And His love doesn't quit when things get ugly, since He loved His own to the very end, even with betrayal already in the room (John 13:1-2).

Then Jesus hands the towel to us. He says, "I have set you an example so that you should do as I have done for you" (John 13:15), and then, "If you know these things, you will be blessed if you do them" (John 13:17). So the blessing is in the doing, baker, not just the knowing. Go find somebody this week and serve them.
